rule.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Execution to Bypass Powershell Restriction
rule.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, OSCD Community

es.summary: Un script block de PowerShell hace referencia a SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe, un binario firmado de App-V que puede ejecutar comandos de PowerShell fuera de powershell.exe. Esto puede indicar un intento de evadir restricciones de ejecución de PowerShell.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 4104 (Script Block Logging) cuyo campo ScriptBlockText contiene la cadena 'SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe'. Requiere que Script Block Logging esté habilitado.
es.why_it_matters: SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe es un LOLBin documentado en LOLBAS: un argumento como "n; <comando>" se ejecuta como código PowerShell. Los atacantes lo usan para eludir bloqueos de powershell.exe o controles de aplicaciones (ATT&CK T1218, System Binary Proxy Execution).
triage_steps: Lea el ScriptBlockText completo y busque argumentos que empiecen con "n;" seguidos de comandos como IEX, DownloadString, Start-Process o contenido codificado.
Si el script está dividido en varios eventos, reconstrúyalo agrupando por ScriptBlockId y ordenando por MessageNumber.
Identifique el usuario y el host (Computer); confirme si el usuario utiliza App-V legítimamente o es una cuenta de servicio esperada.
Busque la creación de SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe (Sysmon 1 o 4688) en el mismo host y revise su CommandLine, ParentImage y procesos hijos.
Revise conexiones de red, consultas DNS y archivos creados en el mismo host dentro de +/- 15 minutos del evento.
Verifique si el cliente App-V está habilitado (Get-AppvStatus) y si el Path del script corresponde a una herramienta corporativa conocida.
Consulte alertas previas del mismo usuario y host, especialmente por bloqueos de PowerShell, AppLocker o descargas sospechosas.
false_positives: Clientes App-V que sincronizan paquetes con el servidor de publicación mediante SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe.
Scripts de administración o despliegue (SCCM, Intune) que gestionan la sincronización de App-V.
Ejercicios de red team o pruebas autorizadas basadas en LOLBAS.
response_steps: Confirme con el responsable del equipo o de App-V si la ejecución estaba prevista; documente la evidencia del script block.
Si el comando ejecuta código no autorizado, aísle el endpoint y conserve memoria, logs de PowerShell y artefactos descargados.
Bloquee los dominios, IP o hashes identificados y busque los mismos indicadores en el resto de la flota.
Si App-V no se usa, restrinja SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe con AppLocker o WDAC; restablezca credenciales si hubo exposición.
es.severity_rationale: Media porque el binario tiene usos legítimos en entornos App-V, pero invocarlo desde PowerShell es una técnica de evasión conocida que requiere revisión.

en.summary: A PowerShell script block references SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe, a signed App-V binary that can run PowerShell commands outside powershell.exe. This may be an attempt to bypass PowerShell execution restrictions.
en.what_it_detects: Event 4104 (Script Block Logging) where ScriptBlockText contains the string 'SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe'. Script Block Logging must be enabled.
en.why_it_matters: SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe is a documented LOLBAS binary: an argument such as "n; <command>" is executed as PowerShell code. Attackers use it to get around powershell.exe blocks or application control (ATT&CK T1218, System Binary Proxy Execution).
triage_steps: Read the full ScriptBlockText and look for arguments starting with "n;" followed by IEX, DownloadString, Start-Process or encoded content.
If the script spans several events, rebuild it by grouping on ScriptBlockId and ordering by MessageNumber.
Identify the user and host (Computer); confirm whether the user legitimately uses App-V or is an expected service account.
Find the SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe process creation (Sysmon 1 or 4688) on the host and review its CommandLine, ParentImage and child processes.
Review network connections, DNS queries and file writes on the same host within +/- 15 minutes.
Check whether the App-V client is enabled (Get-AppvStatus) and whether the script Path matches a known corporate tool.
Look for earlier alerts for the same user and host, especially PowerShell, AppLocker blocks or suspicious downloads.
false_positives: App-V clients syncing packages with the publishing server through SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe.
Administration or deployment scripts (SCCM, Intune) that manage App-V synchronization.
Authorized red team exercises or LOLBAS-based testing.
response_steps: Confirm with the host owner or App-V team whether the execution was expected; preserve the script block evidence.
If unauthorized code ran, isolate the endpoint and collect memory, PowerShell logs and any downloaded artifacts.
Block identified domains, IPs or hashes and hunt for the same indicators across the fleet.
If App-V is unused, restrict SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe with AppLocker or WDAC; reset credentials if exposure occurred.
en.severity_rationale: Medium because the binary has legitimate App-V uses, but invoking it from PowerShell is a known evasion technique that warrants review.

positive.description: PowerShell script uses SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe to proxy a download-and-execute command
Direct invocation of the binary with a PowerShell command argument

negative.description: Legitimate App-V management cmdlets with no reference to the executable
Script references the VBS variant, not the .exe, so the contains match fails
